summary: git_push: the shared host bare clone is locked only on first clone, not on fetch/push
description:
Source: DFMEA 2026-11-04 (F09). Confirmed: `tools/git_push.py` takes `network-heavy` only for the first `clone --bare`. The later `fetch`, bundle import, `update-ref` and `push` on `%LOCALAPPDATA%/anvil/repos/<repo>` run unlocked, so two runs pushing the same repo can hit `*.lock` errors or interleave refs.

Today the build lock usually serialises runs, so this is rare, but the API itself allows parallel runs.

**Fix:** hold a per-repo lock (`acquire_lock(f"git-push-{repo}")`) across the whole fetch → import → check → push sequence.

**Acceptance:** a test where two concurrent `git_push` calls on one repo both succeed.

comments.body: [devin] PR #87 up: https://github.com/vishal7pandey/anvil/pull/87 — acquire_lock(git-push-<repo>) wraps the whole fetch->import->check->push sequence on the shared host clone (was locked only for first clone --bare). Test: two concurrent pushes on one repo both land. 11 passed.
